headline: Fakhrul and Oli to contest presidential election on Aug 20
summary: The Election Commission has confirmed that neither candidate has withdrawn, clearing the way for a vote among 349 lawmakers on Thursday.
details: BNP’s Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and LDP’s Oli Ahmed will contest the presidential election on August 20, as no candidate has withdrawn their nomination paper.
The election will take place at the parliament from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm, according to EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, serving as the returning officer, will oversee the process and welcome the 349 lawmakers to cast their votes.
Ballot papers will be printed in black and white, featuring a counterfoil for voter identification and a voting portion with candidates' names listed alphabetically.
Ballots will be counted immediately after 5:00 pm, and the candidate with the highest number of valid votes will be declared the preliminary winner.
The High Court has also rejected a writ seeking the suspension of the election schedule and a challenge to Article 70, ensuring the process proceeds as planned.
caption:
Two candidates remain in the race for the presidency. The vote takes place this Thursday.

BNP’s Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and LDP’s Oli Ahmed will contest the presidential election on August 20, as no candidate has withdrawn their nomination paper.

The election will take place at the parliament from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm, according to EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed.

Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, serving as the returning officer, will oversee the process and welcome the 349 lawmakers to cast their votes.

Ballot papers will be printed in black and white, featuring a counterfoil for voter identification and a voting portion with candidates' names listed alphabetically.

Ballots will be counted immediately after 5:00 pm, and the candidate with the highest number of valid votes will be declared the preliminary winner.

The High Court has also rejected a writ seeking the suspension of the election schedule and a challenge to Article 70, ensuring the process proceeds as planned.

headline: 753 hospitalised as 3 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a rise in fatalities and hospitalisations across the country.
details: At least three dengue patients died and 753 others were hospitalised across Bangladesh in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the deaths occurred in Dhaka North City Corporation, Khulna, and Mymensingh divisions.
This latest surge brings the total number of dengue deaths this year to 753.
The total number of reported dengue cases nationwide has now reached 25,601.
